chaptersSub: Chapters follow the textbook, Building Toward Calculus. Hover over an outcome to see its full statement, and select one to open its page.

fluency.title: Foundational Fluency
fluency.lead: These are the skills every chapter leans on: solving equations, exponents, fractions, and right triangles. They come from Chapter 6 of the textbook and the practice we do in class. If your algebra is getting in the way, start here, any week.

toolsSub: The things you will reach for in every chapter.

tools.name: Textbook: Building Toward Calculus
tools.description: The free course textbook on LibreTexts, with readings, activities, and online exercises for every outcome.

tools.name: CheckIt support hub

tools.name: Desmos graphing calculator

help.title: When you are stuck
help.sub: Name the kind of stuck you are in. Each one starts somewhere different.

paths.title: I do not understand the idea
paths.text: Open the outcome page. Read the textbook section, then work through the FAQ and guided learning for that outcome.

paths.title: I cannot start a CheckIt problem
paths.text: Open the CheckIt support page for the outcome. Read the quick summary, then follow a worked example that matches your problem.

paths.title: I keep making the same mistake
paths.text: Try Spot the Slip on the CheckIt support page: find the error in someone else's work. Then ask the Practice Partner for a similar problem.

paths.title: My algebra is getting in the way
paths.text: That is common, and fixable. Go to Foundational Fluency and pick the skill that tripped you up.

paths.title: I am behind or overwhelmed
paths.text: You do not have to sort it out alone. Talk to a person, or ask for help with basic needs.

ai.title: AI study partner
ai.sub: AI can support your learning when you use it thoughtfully. Try the problem yourself first, then use AI to get unstuck, check your thinking, and practice.

partner.name: Math 172 Practice Partner
partner.text: Paste a problem you are working on and the Practice Partner gives you similar problems at the level you pick, from a warm-up to a challenge. Ask it for a critique problem and it shows a worked solution with an error for you to find. It runs on Playlab, so it is free to use.

ai.stepsTitle: How to use AI to learn
steps: Try the problem first. Write down what you tried and where you got stuck.
Tell the AI what you tried, not just the problem. Ask for a hint or a question, not the answer.
If it gives you the whole answer, type: "Do not solve it for me. Ask me one question at a time."
Check what it says against the textbook or the CheckIt support page. AI can be wrong.
Finish with a new problem you solve on your own, so you know you can do it without help.
ai.faqNote: Each outcome's FAQ and guided learning page also has AI prompts written for that outcome.

people.title: Still stuck? Talk to a person
